parsed.why: No trans-specific offence, entry-easing programme, documented social acceptance and mature care industry; negatives are thin enforcement of the GI discrimination act, no hate-crime law, and custody/ward placement risks that bite mainly if detained or hospitalised.

Morality offences de-facto criminalise gender nonconformity and transition, no recognition or protections, registered groups barred, and militias have tortured and executed effeminate or 'gay'-accused people with no recourse. State-tolerated targeting plus penal exposure.

Tier-1 state exposure: entry cable flags document discrepancies, federal passports cannot be made to match, and many states exclude or criminalise facility use (documented arrest, men's-ward hold). Protective states, hate-crime coverage and court injunctions partially mitigate.

No criminalisation, recognition achievable via medical certificate, partnerships in force; negatives are hate-crime impunity (court found violations, prosecutor reopened) and no GI discrimination law. Silent on police, facilities and border practice in a well-documented state.

Unenforced sodomy and public 'impersonation' offences plus no recognition or protections, an activist murdered in 2021, and rising fundamentalist hostility with no documented recourse; an embedded third-gender tradition and zero recent prosecutions keep it out of the upper bands.
